headline: A tech-led stock slump sends CGBs to new lows; the belly leads as the 10Y nears 1.62%
summary: CGBs rallied again on Thursday as Chinese tech stocks slumped. The CCDC 10-year fell 1.1bp to 1.623% and the 30-year 0.2bp to 2.047%, both 1-year lows, while the belly led: the 7-year dropped 1.7bp to 1.431% and the 5-year 1.1bp to 1.330%, so 10s30s steepened 0.9bp to 42.3bp. Policy banks lagged slightly: CDB 10-year fell 0.9bp to 1.661%, 3.8bp over CGB, with ADBC and EXIM about 6.6bp and 5.7bp over.
drivers: The ChiNext fell 4.45% and the STAR 50 about 4.3% as AI hardware and chip stocks slid after Alphabet's miss and weak Samsung chip profits; the Shanghai Composite lost 0.82% to 3,651 on RMB1.56tn turnover. Wednesday's bond profit-taking reversed, with T futures up 0.11% and TL up 0.09%.

The PBOC rolled RMB1tn of overnight repos and added RMB115bn of 7-day repos at 1.40%, a RMB115bn net injection. DR001 held near 1.28% and overnight Shibor at 1.282%, so carry stays cheap into the Nov 2 end of the overnight series and the expected switch to an overnight policy rate.

With the active 10-year (260016) at about 1.61%, dealers report banks turning sellers and funds taking profit, and several desks expect a range until the new DR001 anchor is set. That limited the 10-year and especially the 30-year, which barely moved.

The Fed held at 3.75–4% with two hawkish dissents and US 10-year yields near 5%, but the yuan sits near a June 2022 high, so there is no external pressure. The plenum focused on Party discipline, not the economy. CDB sold 3-year and 10-year bonds at 1.337% and 1.652% with 4.3x and 7.6x cover, while Industrial Securities sees about RMB2.5tn of net government bond supply in Nov–Dec.
data: Q3 PBOC loan report (Oct 28)
Property loans RMB50.08tn, −5.2% y/y; mortgages RMB35.91tn, −4.1% y/y (−1.1tn YTD)
Households keep paying down mortgages, so credit demand stays weak and banks keep buying bonds.
Sep industrial profits (Oct 27)
A beat driven by AI hardware, metals and oil-linked prices, not households; bonds looked through it.
Oct MLF (Oct 26)
RMB700bn 1Y vs RMB900bn maturing (net −200bn); outright reverse repos +400bn net in Oct
A tidy-up, not tightening: medium-term liquidity is still up RMB200bn in October, and the overnight rate is now the policy signal.
Q3 GDP (Oct 19)
Firmer growth, near the bottom of the 4.5–5% target. It eases pressure for stimulus but was not strong enough to sell bonds.
Sep activity (Oct 19)
Growth is led by exports and AI-linked output, with households and property still weak. It does not challenge low yields.
Sep CPI / PPI (Oct 14)
CPI 0.9% (f 1.0%), core 1.0%; PPI 5.0% (f 4.4–4.5%), highest since Jun 2022
Cost-push from oil and AI components, not demand. Bonds ignore it unless core CPI follows.
Sep credit (Oct 14)
New loans RMB1.08tn (f 0.98tn); TSF 3.55tn; M2 7.2% (f 7.4%); M1 3.2%
Loan growth is at a record-low 4.8% and money growth is slowing. Weak credit demand keeps banks buying bonds.
view: Mildly bullish for the next 1–2 weeks, with the 10-year expected in a 1.59–1.65% CCDC range. The tech selloff, overnight cash at the RMB1tn cap and a likely overnight policy rate near 1.25% from Nov 2 support duration, but banks selling near 1.60% and Nov–Dec supply cap the long end. I prefer 10-year CGBs over the rich 5–7Y belly and over policy banks, and stay neutral on the 30-year. An overnight rate at or below 1.25% or a soft October PMI would take the 10-year toward 1.59–1.60%; an equity rebound or a heavy November supply calendar would push it back to 1.65%.

buckets.name: CGB 1–2Y
buckets.why: The 2-year fell 1.1bp to 1.222%, a 1-year low (0th percentile, average 1.312%), and the 1-year at 1.165% is about 12bp below overnight Shibor (1.282%). The front end already prices an overnight policy rate near 1.25%.
buckets.call: Hold; don't chase below 1.20% on the 2-year. Add only if the overnight rate is set below 1.25%.

buckets.name: CGB 5–7Y belly
buckets.why: The 5-year (1.330%) and 7-year (1.431%) set new lows, and the 2s5s10s fly is −18.6bp, a 1-year low (0th percentile, average −7.5bp); 5s7s10s is −9.2bp (1st percentile). The 5s10s flattener from ~29bp is open and flat at 29.4bp (81st percentile, average 26.4bp), inside the 31bp stop.
buckets.call: Keep the 5Y-into-10Y switch (5s10s flattener) from ~29bp, target 25bp, stop 31bp.

buckets.name: CGB 10Y
buckets.why: The 10-year fell 1.1bp to 1.623%, a 1-year low, but against its neighbours it is still cheap: the 7s10s20s fly is −21.8bp, in the 96th percentile against a −29.3bp average. The buy level (1.65–1.66%) was not reached and the 1.61% take-profit is 1bp away.
buckets.call: Range 1.59–1.65%. Buy on a back-up to 1.645–1.65%; take profit near 1.61%.

buckets.name: CGB 30Y
buckets.why: 10s30s steepened 0.9bp to 42.3bp, in the 25th percentile and below its 45.5bp average, as the 30-year lagged with a 0.2bp fall to 2.047%. Weak credit demand supports it, but it is the most crowded trade and supply is due in November.
buckets.call: Neutral. Add above 2.10% (10s30s ~46bp); poor risk/reward below 2.05%.

buckets.name: Policy banks 2–10Y vs CGB
buckets.why: CDB 10-year is 3.8bp over CGB, in the 3rd percentile against a 10.0bp average, and CDB 2-year and 5-year spreads (13.3bp and 10.0bp) sit in the 3rd percentiles. The switch from ~3bp is open and slightly in the money (+0.8bp); policy banks lagged today's rally despite solid CDB auctions.
buckets.call: Keep the CDB 10Y into CGB 10Y switch from ~3bp, target 8bp, stop 1bp.

buckets.name: ADBC/EXIM vs CDB 10Y
buckets.why: ADBC 10-year yields 2.9bp more than CDB, in the 73rd percentile against a 1.2bp average; EXIM is 1.9bp over, at its 2.0bp average. Recent ADBC and CDB auctions drew strong cover, so the pickup is about supply and liquidity, not credit.
buckets.call: Hold ADBC/EXIM 10Y rather than CDB 10Y for the ~2–3bp pickup.

buckets.name: Policy banks 20–30Y
buckets.why: CDB 20-year is 6.4bp over CGB and the 30-year 11.0bp, both at the bottom of their 1-year ranges (averages 10.8bp and 12.8bp). Policy bank long bonds simply track CGBs, so there is no spread cushion if supply picks up.
buckets.call: Prefer CGB 20–30Y to CDB 20–30Y; revisit policy bank long bonds above a 13bp 30-year spread.

watch: Next: October PMIs (Sat Oct 31), the end of the overnight repo series and the overnight policy rate the PBOC sets (Nov 2), Hong Kong accepting CGBs as margin collateral from Nov 2, the US midterms (Nov 3), November MoF and local bond calendars, then October trade, inflation and credit data.
sources: Xinhua Finance via Sina (bond daily, Oct 29)
